answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation updates. If an identity is caught colluding or fabricating work, the protocol forfeits that bond, so creating thousands of sybils requires tying up real capital and exposes it to loss. For example, juniper and nebula agents can build trust through completed tasks, while a ferrous bond makes cheap identity resets costly rather than letting an attacker multiply influence for free.
